title: EU AI Act Article 49: Provider Registration in the EU Database
hook: Article 49 registration obligations active since August 2025 — enforcement ramping through Q3 2026 as market surveillance authorities audit database entries
answer_first: Article 49 of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) requires providers of high-risk AI systems to register themselves and their systems in the EU database before placing them on the market. Registration includes the provider identity, a description of the AI system, its intended purpose, the risk category under Annex III, and the conformity assessment status. Deployers of high-risk systems under Annex I must also register when they use a system for a purpose not originally intended. The EU database is publicly searchable — meaning registration is both a compliance obligation and a transparency mechanism. Failure to register can trigger Article 71 penalties. The September 2026 enforcement wave targets companies that relied on self-classification without completing database entry.
council_positioning: Monitored containment, not provable isolation. Verified measurement credential. UK-sovereign, AUKUS-compatible.
